library_preparation_preflight.summary: Moments/TimeMachine need org.springframework.context.ApplicationEventPublisher, but spring-context is absent from spring-modulith-moments's own POM (normally supplied transitively via spring-boot-starter when consumed through spring-modulith-starter-core); a standalone test won't compile without it.

library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: Exercise the module via org.springframework.modulith.moments.support.TimeMachine, which is the public, test-facing subclass of Moments (shiftBy(Duration) and reset() are public overrides specifically meant for tests; on Moments itself they are package-private). Construct it with Clock.fixed(...), a simple test ApplicationEventPublisher (a List-collecting lambda/anonymous implementation is enough — no Mockito needed), and MomentsProperties.DEFAULTS (its constructors are private, but DEFAULTS is a public static field, so no Spring Boot config-binding machinery is required). Call shiftBy(Duration) with values crossing hour/day/week/month/quarter/year boundaries and assert the published event types (HourHasPassed, DayHasPassed, WeekHasPassed, MonthHasPassed, QuarterHasPassed, YearHasPassed). No database, Docker image, environment variable, or system property is needed — this module is a pure in-memory time/event abstraction.
risks: The missing spring-context dependency appears to be a gap/quirk in the published POM for this module rather than intentional design; worth a quick sanity check against a newer patch version in case upstream fixes it, though 2.1.0 is the version requested here.

Local Gradle compilation and the native-image agent run remain authoritative — if compileTestJava succeeds without the added dependency for some unforeseen transitive reason, drop it rather than keeping unused setup.
